question: Let $f$ and $g$ be two non-decreasing twice differentiable functions defined on an interval $(a,b)$ such that for each $x\in(a,b)$, $f''(x)=g(x)$ and $g''(x)=f(x)$. Suppose also that $f(x)g(x)$ is linear in $x$ on $(a,b)$. Show that we must have $f(x)=g(x)=0$ for all $x\in(a,b)$.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
